title: Why Planes Fly in a Curve on the Map
lines: On a flat map, a flight from New York to Tokyo looks way too curved.
So why doesn't the plane just fly in a straight line?
Because the Earth isn't flat. It's a ball.
And a flat map stretches everything near the poles.
On the globe, the shortest path between two cities bends toward the pole.
It's called a great circle route.
So the curved line is actually shorter than the straight one, and saves a lot of fuel.
The curve is the shortcut. Follow for more!
caption:
Why do flights look curved on the map? 🌍✈️ The Earth is a sphere, and flat maps stretch everything near the poles. The real shortest path between two cities is a 'great circle' route — that's why flights from New York to Tokyo go over Alaska.
